_what: How build-reports/person-index.json is rebuilt WITHOUT losing the work of scripts that patch it after the claims build. Read by src/build_person_index.py (which runs the chain) and src/gate_person_index.py (which refuses a rebuild if any writer is missing from here).
_why: On 2026-09-06 a rebuild silently discarded 60 CFL 1945 seasons, 476 club-key rewrites, 2,576 coaching seasons and 1,052 officiating records, because five scripts wrote the index directly and nothing recorded that they must be re-run. It was caught only because one session measured season-holders before and after by hand.

chain.adds: club-key normalisation from build/club-key-normalisation.json; marks each rewritten season with _club_as_printed
chain.must_precede: apply_person_merges.py -- its own docstring: the index must be normalised BEFORE merging, because merges union seasons by key

chain.adds: declarations/person-merge-decisions.json (the decisions, in git since 2026-09-11), RE-applied: the builder applies merges at build time, but club-key normalisation runs after that and may change keys, so merges are applied again (undo-then-apply, idempotent)
chain.must_precede: apply_promotions.py -- the promotion decisions were made against the MERGED index (promote_coaches.py: 'checked_against ... AFTER the 92 merges'); applying them before merges could attach a season to an absorbed record

chain.adds: coaching_seasons, entered_by, promotion_ref, _playing_fields_do_not_apply from build/coach-promotions.json; creates the coaching-only people
entered_by, promotion_ref, forename_unknown and _entered_as_a_player for the players promoted from document leads in build/player-promotions.json
chain.must_follow: apply_promotions.py -- one mechanism, two subject types, and the coach route runs first because its promotions can create people this one then reads past
chain._it_does_not_own_seasons: a promoted player's seasons come from the ingest's CLAIMS (resolve_person returns any P_ id as itself), so unlike apply_promotions this step owns only the promotion metadata. It counts promoted_but_holding_none rather than creating a season, so a promotion whose claims did not land is visible instead of papered over.

chain.adds: reverses the 201 promoted coaches with no coaching stint (build/coach-demotions.json)
the 60 CFL 1945 season keys the ingest never wrote as stints (build/cfl1945-season-restore.json)
chain.runs_last_because: it writes final-form keys CFL|1945|CFLCGY and CFL|1945|CFLWPG and skips a key already present; club-key-normalisation.json does rewrite CFLCGY/CFLWPG codes (though no 1945 entry today), so running AFTER normalisation guarantees the restored keys are never un-normalised or duplicated

chain.adds: the 978 officials created by ingest_officials.py (name, roles, officiating_seasons, identified_by.officials_pfa_code) plus officiating_seasons on the 74 players who already existed -- 1,052 men from build/pfa-officials.json
chain.runs_last_because: MEASURED, not assumed: today it has no hard dependency on any earlier step -- 0 official ids are absorbed by a person-merge, 0 collide with a promoted coach id, 0 share a person_id or a PFA code with the 201 demoted coaches, and officials carry no playing seasons for apply_club_keys to rewrite. It is placed last because that is the position that stays correct if any of those becomes non-zero: running after the merges attaches officiating to the surviving record rather than an absorbed one, and running after demote_stintless re-establishes as an OFFICIAL any man that step removes as a coach, which is what Ryan's ruling requires.
chain.idempotent: YES, in both directions. Every value is a pure function of build/pfa-officials.json and is SET rather than skipped, so a fresh index and a half-applied one converge to the same result. Its report is built from all 1,052 men every run rather than from that run's delta -- which is the specific way apply_promotions.py is NOT idempotent: run by hand against an index that already holds its ids it writes an EMPTY coach-seasons-promoted.json over a good one.
chain.own_output_not_covered_by_rollback: build/officials-applied.json. The rollback restores the INDEX only, so after a rollback this report describes a run that was undone. Re-running the script fixes it.

_order_note: Steps 1->2, 2->3 and 3->4 are hard dependencies (see must_precede). Step 5's position is a safety rule, not a hard dependency today: with the current normalisation file either position gives the same index. Keep it last anyway.

exempt.index_io.py: the atomic-write helper itself; every writer above goes through save_index

how_a_new_patcher_is_picked_up: It is not picked up automatically -- it FAILS LOUDLY. gate_person_index.py scans every src/*.py for a write to the index (open(<index>,'w'), save_index(, dump_atomic(...,<index>)). Any writer not named in `chain` or `exempt` fails P1 by filename with the offending line, and build_person_index.py refuses to rebuild while P1 fails. To add a patcher: write it using index_io.save_index, then add it to `chain` in the right position with `must_precede` / `adds` filled in.
_known_missing_steps_note: Emptied 2026-09-06: the officials applier that was recorded here is now src/apply_officials.py, step 6 of the chain.

held_stores._what: stores the builder reads, COUNTS and REPORTS but does not index, pending a ruling. Not a silent skip: build_person_index prints them and writes them to build-reports/person-index-skipped.json on every build.

store_league_tokens._what: build_person_index derives a stint's league from the STORE FILENAME (stats-nfl-1987 -> NFL). A store whose name is not its league is declared here.
store_league_tokens.assistants: COACHES -- the media guides' staff lists are coaching seasons, and they must land on the same key shape as the Coaching Tree's so a guide's role string attaches to the season it corroborates rather than opening a parallel ASSISTANTS league. Declared 2026-09-07 with Ryan's ruling that a club's own guide naming a man as its coach documents that he worked that season.
store_league_tokens.programme-1926-chi-lat: NFL -- the store is one DOCUMENT, not a league. Its Bears claims are corroboration for club-seasons the archive already holds, so they must land on NFL|1925|CHI. Without this the filename token opened a parallel PROGRAMME league and Red Grange gained a PROGRAMME|1925|CHI season beside his real one -- the same failure this block was created to stop for `assistants`. Found 2026-09-07 by reading the index after the rebuild, not before it. Carries Ryan's ruling that the Bears corroboration joins NFL|1925|CHI.
store_league_tokens.programme-1926-nyy-pcw: AFL -- the store is one DOCUMENT, not a league. Its ten corroborating claims must land on AFL|1926|AFLPC, the club-season they confirm. Without this the filename token would open a parallel PROGRAMME league, exactly as it did for programme-1926-chi-lat before that store was declared.
store_league_tokens.ghostsofthegridiron: NFL -- Fenton's NFL-era rosters. A store carries ONE league and this source covers two, so it is split; the AFL half is ghostsofthegridiron-afl.
store_league_tokens.ghostsofthegridiron-afl: AFL -- the 1926 Philadelphia Quakers roster. Without this the filename token would put them on an NFL key and the eight positions this page fills would land on a club-season that does not exist.
store_league_tokens.ghostsofthegridiron-ind: IND -- NOT A LEAGUE. Frankford's 1922 and 1923 independent seasons assert no league at all; the club table carries the club with an EMPTY league, as it already does for six PFA independents. The index key needs a token in the league position and there is no way to write an empty one, so IND is that token and means 'independent, no league asserted'. It must never be read as a competition and no club-season outside this store may use it.
store_league_tokens.pfa-wlaf-1995: WLAF -- the store is named for its SOURCE and its season, so the filename's first token is `pfa`, which is not a league. The 45 men are the 1995 Scottish Claymores of the World League of American Football, the same league the archive holds for 1991 and 1992. Declared 2026-09-08 rather than renaming the file, because the store's name says truthfully where it came from.

store_league_tokens.salaries: SALARIES -- NOT A LEAGUE, and the token exists only because the index needs one. This follows the IND precedent exactly, which declarations/clubs.json states outright: build_person_index writes a season key as (league, year, club) and has no way to write an empty league, so a store asserting none needs a token and the token is declared. The store is a COURT RECORD about pay; its season keys read `y1975` and name no league anywhere. Declaring it as a single-word token means RS-G7 exempts it the way it exempts IND, COACHES and DRAFT, and the 15 men whose keys read `SALARIES|y1975|...` keep them. Ruled 2026-09-09 after the empty-league form broke both P3 and apply_club_keys' normalisation.

derived_tables_after_the_chain._what: Scripts that read the FINISHED, P3-proved index and build a derived artifact from it. They are part of the rebuild -- if one fails, the rebuild fails and rolls back -- but they are not index patchers and P1 must not treat them as such.
derived_tables_after_the_chain._the_property: Every script here exists, and NONE of them writes the index. That is the inverse of P1's rule for `chain`, and it is checked, not assumed: a derived table that quietly wrote the index would be a patcher wearing the wrong label and P3 would see its work as an unexplained gain.
derived_tables_after_the_chain._why_after_P3: A derived table built from an index that lost work would carry the loss forward and look fine. P3 proves nothing fell first.

steps.adds: build/clubs.json -- the club table, rebuilt from the FINISHED index so it can never be older than the claims that feed it
steps.must_follow: every step above it. build_clubs reads build-reports/person-index.json in its final state, and it imports apply_club_keys and apply_person_merges to UNDO their layers itself (it needs the pre-merge view to test lineage). Running it earlier would hand it an index the chain had not finished patching, and it would undo layers that were not yet applied.
steps._why_it_is_here: Ryan's ruling 2026-09-07: the club table must never be silently older than the claims that feed it. It was in NO chain and NO gate ran it, so it sat frozen from the machine move on 2026-09-07 until 22:00 that night -- and it could not have run anyway, because its fandom-survey path was hardcoded to the laptop's Dropbox. Nothing was red. A club written, indexed and served was invisible to search_clubs and the omission looked exactly like success.
steps._it_can_now_fail_the_rebuild: Deliberate. If the club table cannot be built the rebuild stops and rolls back, rather than publishing claims against a stale table. That is the ruling's whole point, and it is why the missing-input refusal in build_clubs now lists every path it tried.
steps._why_not_in_the_chain: P1 requires every `chain` step to WRITE THE INDEX, and it was right to refuse this one. build_clubs.py is not an index patcher: it CONSUMES the finished index and writes a different artifact. Forcing it into `chain` would have meant weakening the property P1 exists to hold. It gets its own phase with the INVERSE property instead -- a derived table must NOT write the index.
steps.runs: after the chain and after P3 has proved nothing fell

p3_one_time_transition._what: The EXACT ids P3 may see disappear on the next rebuild, and only while _enabled is true. EMPTY and disabled: the last use is recorded in p3_transitions_completed under 2026-09-11-ghosts-lineup-shells.

_chain_args_note: Every chain step is now invoked with --write. Ruled 2026-09-09: a script must not write unless asked, so the five that used to write on a bare run now need the flag -- and the chain must pass it or the rebuild would run them, they would compute, write nothing, and P3 would see the index lose everything they were supposed to apply. Changing the scripts without changing this would have been worse than the property it fixes.

pseudo_league_tokens._what: Single-word tokens `store_league_tokens` declares that are NOT competitions. The index writes a season key as (league, year, club) and has no way to write an empty league, so a store asserting none needs a token; these are those tokens. Anything reading a season key to decide what league to hand the club resolver must read THIS, not a typed pair.
pseudo_league_tokens._why: Measured 2026-09-09: `('COACHES', 'SALARIES')` was typed out in four places -- clubs.py, gate_clubs.py, normalise_club_keys.py and build_clubs.PSEUDO -- while this declaration already held the answer. `IND` was declared a non-competition on 2026-09-08 and added to none of the four, so 69 season keys have been handing the club resolver `IND` as though it were a league ever since. A third pseudo-league is only safe when the list is read rather than typed.
pseudo_league_tokens._derived_not_typed: gate_clubs.py K10 recomputes this set as (single-word tokens in store_league_tokens) MINUS (leagues the club table holds) and fails if it differs, so the list cannot drift from the declaration it summarises.
